page.layout: Running head at top centre above the text block (one line, "218 DE ANNO, MENSE, ET DIE" with page number at left). Main text in one column, full width, top to bottom. Then a full-width rule, then the large centred title "APPENDIX PRIMA" with subtitle line. Then the text of §. I, with a decorated initial "E" at left, running in one column to the foot of the page.

main_text.l: TI. KAISAP, in parte aversâ IOTAIA L. A. Alter
est Antiochenus apud Tristanum, exhibens Tiberii
caput laureatum cum verbis TI. KAISAP ΣEBAΣTOΣ
APXIEP. MEГ. Tiberius Cæsar Augustus Pont. Maximus:
in parte aversâ legitur APXIEPATIKON ANTIOXEIΣ A.
quod ipse vir doctus exponit Sacrorum principatum apud
se ANTIOCHENI Tiberio deferunt anno
ejus primo. Quis non hinc mecum agnoscat, non fuis-
se morem in Oriente, in nummis magis omittere primum
Augustorum annum, quam reliquorum numeros,
quoniam primum Tiberii in tribus nummis confignatum
cernimus.
APPENDIX
PRIMA

l.i: Aliquot nummos cum eorundem expositione referens.

main_text.l: §. I. EXhibet tabula nostra prima nummos Præ-
sidum Syriæ novem, quorum tres priores
sub Quintilio Varo, quinque sequentes
sub Silano, cusi sunt, atque ultimus seu nonus
sub Flacco. Hi omnes æram cum Antiochenam
tum Seleucienses in annis signatis referentes, ostendunt
eas civitates (circa Christi tempora & post) æram
actiacam assumpsisse, atque annos suos ab Asiâ receptâ
putasse: cujus æræ annus primus concurrit cum anno
Nabonassaris 718. Olymp. 187 : 2. Scilicet à iv Non
Sept.

page.notes: The initial "E" of §. I is a large woodcut initial, transcribed as "E" joined to "Xhibet". Coin legends in the first paragraph are set in capitals with Greek words (ΣEBAΣTOΣ, APXIEP. MEГ., APXIEPATIKON ANTIOXEIΣ) reproduced as printed; the Greek letters are uncertain at places and the Σ/E forms in the printed legend may be doubtful, so verify against the scan. Word "IOTAIA" and "Tristanum" are as printed. Possible printing errors: "Antiochenam" (§. I) appears to be printed as such. "Seleucienses" is printed as "Seleuciensem" in the scan; transcribed as printed. The left-hand dot mark on the page edge and show-through are not transcribed. Greek lettering in the first paragraph is only partly legible; where a letter could not be read with certainty it should be checked.
